primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Loss of tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase activity from ALPL pathogenic variants prevents normal hydrolysis of extracellular inorganic pyrophosphate. Accumulated pyrophosphate inhibits hydroxyapatite crystal growth and mineralization of bone and teeth.
vignette: A 4-year-old child is evaluated for bowed legs and delayed motor milestones. Several primary incisors were lost without trauma, and the roots remained attached to the shed teeth. Radiographs show rachitic metaphyseal changes. Serum calcium and phosphate are within the expected range, but serum alkaline phosphatase activity is persistently low for age and pyridoxal 5'-phosphate is elevated.
lead: Which biochemical abnormality most directly causes the defective skeletal mineralization in this child?
correct: Accumulation of extracellular inorganic pyrophosphate because of deficient tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase activity
distractors: Excess FGF23 signaling that reduces renal phosphate reabsorption
Reduced conversion of vitamin D to calcitriol because of CYP27B1 deficiency
Production of structurally abnormal type I collagen
Failure of osteoclast proton secretion and resorption-pit acidification
distractor_notes: Excess FGF23 causes phosphate wasting in disorders such as X-linked hypophosphatemia. Hypophosphatasia instead has low alkaline phosphatase activity and impaired breakdown of extracellular pyrophosphate.

CYP27B1 deficiency causes vitamin D-dependent rickets type 1A by reducing calcitriol synthesis, typically lowering calcium and phosphate; it does not explain persistently low alkaline phosphatase with root-intact premature tooth loss.
Abnormal type I collagen is a major mechanism of osteogenesis imperfecta and causes bone fragility, but it does not produce the low-alkaline-phosphatase/pyrophosphate phenotype of hypophosphatasia.

Defective osteoclast acidification can cause osteopetrosis by preventing bone resorption, producing abnormally dense bone rather than a primary mineralization defect from low tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase.
key_expl: Premature loss of primary teeth with intact roots, rachitic changes, and persistently low alkaline phosphatase activity are characteristic of hypophosphatasia. ALPL encodes tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase. When its activity is deficient, inorganic pyrophosphate accumulates extracellularly. Pyrophosphate inhibits hydroxyapatite crystal growth, impairing mineralization of bone and teeth.
objective: Recognize hypophosphatasia from low alkaline phosphatase, premature root-intact tooth loss, and defective mineralization, and link ALPL/TNSALP deficiency to extracellular pyrophosphate accumulation.
clues: premature nontraumatic loss of primary incisors with intact roots
persistently low alkaline phosphatase for age

sources.title: Hypophosphatasia
sources.locator: Summary; Diagnosis — Suggestive Findings; Clinical Description; Molecular Genetics / Pathogenesis
sources.support: GeneReviews characterizes hypophosphatasia by defective bone/tooth mineralization with low alkaline phosphatase activity, premature loss of primary teeth often with intact roots, elevated PLP and inorganic pyrophosphate, and ALPL pathogenic variants.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.title: Hypophosphatasia
sources.support: MedlinePlus states that ALPL encodes tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase and that reduced TNSALP permits inorganic pyrophosphate to accumulate; PPi buildup underlies defective mineralization of bones and teeth.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.title: X-linked hypophosphatemia
sources.support: MedlinePlus states that PHEX variants increase FGF23, reducing intestinal phosphate absorption and renal phosphate reabsorption and causing hypophosphatemic skeletal disease.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.title: Vitamin D-dependent rickets
sources.support: MedlinePlus states that CYP27B1 variants impair conversion of vitamin D to calcitriol and can produce hypocalcemia and hypophosphatemia with defective mineralization.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.title: Osteogenesis imperfecta
sources.support: MedlinePlus states that COL1A1/COL1A2 variants commonly cause osteogenesis imperfecta by reducing or structurally altering type I collagen, producing bone fragility.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.title: TCIRG1 gene
sources.locator: Normal Function; Health Conditions Related to Genetic Changes — Osteopetrosis
sources.support: MedlinePlus states that osteoclast V-ATPase proton secretion acidifies the bone-resorption compartment and that TCIRG1 loss prevents acidification and bone breakdown, causing osteopetrosis.
